newsitem.title: UK: UK Camelot directors consider resigning.
newsitem.headline: UK Camelot directors consider resigning.

text.p: The chairman and three top directors of British lottery operator Camelot Group Plc are strongly considering resigning on Friday in a row with the government over their company bonuses, a spokeswoman said on Thursday.
"The only solution at the moment seems to be for them to resign," said the spokeswoman. "It's not absolutely decided but the directors feel they have been put in an impossible situation."

The spokeswoman said a final decision on the future of chairman Sir George Russell, chief executive Tim Holley, finance director Peter Murphy and communications director David Rigg would be made after a shareholders' meeting and board meeting were held on Friday.
"The only option we are considering at the moment is resignation," she said. Earlier the company had said media reports that the three executives could quit in the row were "speculative".
Camelot has been at the centre of a political storm this week after bonuses inflated its annual executive salary bill 40 percent last year, while sums raised for good causes fell.

Chris Smith, the cabinet minister responsible for the arts and culture, wants executives to hand over some or all of their controversial six-figure bonuses to charity. He has demanded a response by the end of the week and also wants a commitment that such bonuses will not be repeated.
Camelot is a consortium of Racal Electronics Plc, De La Rue Plc, GTECH, Cadbury Schweppes Plc and Fujitsu Ltd's ICL.
Russell told Smith this week that the consortium would examine ways of turning the lottery into a not-for-profit operation.
But some of the consortium's shareholders are reported to oppose the plan.
